findings.title: Unbounded reject-log reads can exhaust ingest memory
findings.what: The log is explicitly append-only, but readRejectSignals reads the entire file as one UTF-8 string, parseRejectSignalLines duplicates it with raw.split('\n'), and every valid record is retained. The 16 KiB check bounds each line only; it does not bound total file bytes, line count, or returned records. Long-lived or externally enlarged logs therefore impose unbounded memory and latency on every read.
findings.fix: Stream the JSONL file line by line and enforce an explicit byte/record budget, preferably retaining only the bounded recent window required by suppression and gold-set consumers.
findings.acceptance: Add a test using a log larger than the configured total-byte or record budget and assert that reading stays within that budget, returns the documented bounded window, and still rejects an individually oversized line.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial second pass re-read src/lib/reject-signals.ts:115-156 and its read-path tests at src/lib/reject-signals.test.ts:113-132. The only enforced bound is per line; neither implementation nor tests impose a total-file/result bound, so the append-only growth case survives.
